While many people look forward to breaks as a chance to unwind, financial anxiety continues to shadow holidaymakers for days or even throughout their entire trip, according to new research.

A survey commissioned by the app thinkmoney revealed that only 27 per cent of travellers who experience money concerns manage to switch off straight away. By the end of their first day away, this figure creeps up to 38 per cent.

However, it typically takes up to three days for the majority of people carrying financial stress to finally leave their worries behind.

By that point, just over half (53 per cent) report that they have successfully managed to relax.

Conversely, more than two-fifths (42 per cent) said they spend most of their getaway trying to switch off, or never fully manage to disconnect at all.

Regional differences were also highlighted in the study. Holidaymakers from the West Midlands are notably unlikely to overcome their money anxieties after the first day, with 66 per cent of those concerned unable to shake off their stress by this stage.

They are followed closely by travellers from the East Midlands and London, where 65 per cent experience the same issue.

Many people look forward to holidays as an opportunity to be carefree and relax - but a survey has found that money worries follow some holidaymakers around for several days of their break or even persist for the whole trip ( PA )

By contrast, people from Wales were particularly likely to say they had put their money worries aside by the end of the first day of their holiday. More than half (56 per cent) of people from Wales with money concerns said they are still worrying after day one of their holiday.

People from some parts of the UK were particularly likely to say they could not shake off their financial worries completely while on holiday.

Nearly half (48 per cent) of financially worried holidaymakers from Scotland said they either take most of their holiday to switch off or never fully manage it. They were closely followed by holidaymakers from Yorkshire and the Humber (47 per cent), according to the research.

More than 2,000 people across the UK were surveyed in June.

The holiday switching off analysis was based on more than 1,000 people in the survey who said they experience money worries while on holiday and provided a definite timeframe for how long it takes them to switch off.

Vix Leyton, a consumer expert at thinkmoney, said: “You can’t put your money worries on airplane mode.

“For some people, the first few days of a holiday are still being spent mentally adding up what they’ve spent, checking whether there’s enough left for the rest of the trip and thinking about the bills waiting at home.”

To help leave money worries at home, Ms Leyton suggested setting a holiday budget, checking which household bills are due to be paid during the trip, and checking banking apps to help prevent overspending while on holiday.

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

News.title: How to have the perfect slow-paced holiday in Zakynthos
News.content:
Zakynthos, also known as Zante, is renowned for raucous nightlife, but there’s a far more authentic side to the Venetians “Fiore di Levante” (Flower of the East). For such a small island, scenery is extremely varied: the southern coastline – home to Laganas’ notorious nightlife strip – also encompasses the pristine beaches of Zakynthos Marine Park, where loggerhead sea turtles come to nest, while some of the island’s best-known attractions, including Navagio Beach on the cliff-lined northerly coast, can only be reached by boat.

Birthplace of the man who penned Greece’s national anthem, Zakynthos was also a magnet for literary greats: Byron lay in state here and philhellene Edgar Allan Poe wrote a sonnet to the island’s “verdant slopes”.

Last but not least, food is a powerful lure here: sit in a rustic sea view tavern sipping local Verdea white wine with a plate full of traditional kouneli stifado – a garlic and tomato-soaked rabbit stew – and you’ll be hooked.

News.title: Ebola doctors ‘step back’ from WHO in drug trial ethics row
News.content:
Two leading doctors have “stepped back” from long-held positions with the World Health Organization amid a row over the ethics of an Ebola drug trial underway in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The randomised control trial, called Ebo-Pep, is testing whether an experimental antiviral is an effective post-exposure treatment.

But experts believe the study’s design puts healthcare workers on the frontline of the epidemic at risk, because it means medics exposed to Ebola might receive a placebo treatment.

“We owe them [healthcare workers] a duty of care to do the best possible thing, and a 50 per cent chance of getting a placebo tablet is not that,” said Prof Tom Fletcher, director of the Global Health Trials Unit at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine. The WHO’s health emergencies clinical unit has also deployed him to Ebola ‘Red Zones’ for more than a decade.

This week, Prof Fletcher and eight other experts based in the UK, US, Uganda, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Canada published their concerns in Nature Africa, calling for a “careful reconsideration” of the trial protocol.

They said they are not against Ebo-Pep or randomised trials, but warned there are “additional ethical obligations” when including healthcare workers in studies like this, given the case fatality rate currently stands at 40 per cent.

Prof Fletcher said: “Ebo-Pep is a really good trial, it’s the trial we’ve talked about doing for years. But we’re talking about [protecting] the ‘one-per-centers’, the people who willingly step into one of the most dangerous environments in the world.”

News.title: Wildfire watch: Inside London’s fire control centre on the hottest day of the year
News.content:
“It’s been relentless, an immense number of calls,” says Yvonne Woodhams, control room commander at the London Fire Brigade’s headquarters on the morning of what turned out to be the hottest day of the year so far.

Inside a nondescript building in South-west London, dozens of fire brigade dispatchers field calls from the public and direct the city’s 5,000 or so firefighters across 102 stations to where they are most needed.

In the middle of another heatwave and on a day when temperatures rose to just above 38 degrees, the control room was busy – the scale and frequency of wildfires in London’s parks and grasslands are now considered unprecedented.

Above the dispatchers there is a live map, with red dots representing each active fire, sprawling from Enfield in the north to Purley in the south.

Wildfires nearly always have a human origin like dropped cigarette butts, glass bottles that magnifies the sunlight, or the now-temporarily banned portable barbecues.

But it’s the tinderbox that London has become which is worrying firefighters.

Scorching hot, low-humidity weather, a bit of wind, and tinder-dry vegetation can cause the smallest spark to ignite an inferno. Conditions like this have been described as “fire weather” by the author John Vaillant.

News.title: Inside the biggest collection of venomous snakes in Latin America
News.content:
On the outskirts of São Paulo, several secure serpentariums sit in forested parkland. They contain some of the most venomous creatures on earth and provide the fuel for Latin America’s biggest antivenom manufacturing and research facility.

In one corner of the grounds, huts on stilts house five of Brazil’s most endangered snakes. One, the golden lancehead, is so rare that poachers asked $20,000 for a single specimen. It is found only on a tiny uninhabited island off the South Atlantic coast.

Nearby, inside the campus’s oldest building, a dip worn into the stone floor shows wear from the original serum-producing horses housed here over a century ago. Around it hang old scientific drawings and shelves stacked with journals bound in snakeskin.

Founded in 1901 by physician Dr Vital Brazil, the institute pioneered the development of species-specific antivenoms Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

This is Brazil’s Butantan Institute. Founded in 1901 to fight an outbreak of bubonic plague, it now produces almost all of the country's antivenoms, supplying at least 350,000 vials annually. It is part of a public health system that has made snakebite in Latin America far less deadly than almost anywhere else in the world.

Now, having spent over a century perfecting antivenom at home, Brazil is expanding its global impact – sharing not just its lifesaving sera, but its world-leading snake research.

Specimens in a jar at the institute Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

More than five million people are bitten by snakes around the world each year. Between 82,000 and 138,000 die, while roughly three times as many suffer amputations or permanent disability, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

The burden falls heaviest on poor rural communities in Asia (up to two million bites annually) and Africa (around 500,000), where farmers, women and children walk through dense vegetation without protective clothing or access to nearby hospitals.

Across the Americas, the incidence of bites is far smaller. Some 57,000 are bitten by snakes each year, with Brazil accounting for over 30,000, according to the country’s health ministry.

But what stands out is the survival rate. According to the Pan American Health Organization (Paho), the region’s fatality rate is just 0.6 per cent – compared to up to 12 per cent in some rural regions of Africa.

Latin American snakes are no less dangerous. Venom from bothrops, a genus of the pit viper known locally as “jaracas”, can dissolve blood vessels, stop clotting and cause severe flesh rot or necrosis. Bites from the viper account for up to 90 per cent of reported envenomings each year in Brazil.

One of the snakes housed by the Institute Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Brazil’s constitution legally obliges the state to provide treatment regardless of cost, resulting in antivenom having come to be seen as an essential public right, rather than a commodity for profit.

For poor rural workers who cannot afford treatment, receiving free antivenom quickly is what prevents a bite from becoming fatal.

Regional biology helps too. Unlike in Asia or Africa, where dozens of disparate snake families complicate treatment, the dominance of the Bothrops in Brazil makes life easier.

It means that rural clinics only need to stock a few versatile antivenoms rather than dozens of hyper-specialised ones. The Butantan Institute makes roughly 400,000 vials annually, more than enough to meet demand.

Yet even such a well-designed system struggles with the country’s unforgiving geography.

The Butantan Institute is home to Latin America’s largest collection of venomous species Credit : Camila Svenson

Covering nearly half of Brazil, the Amazon rainforest has vast roadless expanses where travel relies on slow wooden boats. For isolated communities, reaching a stocked clinic can take 12 to 24 hours – often beyond the critical window to prevent amputation or death.

Part of the challenge lies in the treatment itself. Traditional liquid antivenom must be administered intravenously under strict medical supervision due to the risk of acute allergic reactions. Crucially, it also requires an unbroken cold chain.

When exposed to tropical heat, the therapeutic proteins quickly denature and clump together. This renders the serum useless or, in the worst cases, dangerous.

Dr Grazziotin holds a tiny snake Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

To overcome this, Brazil is increasingly deploying freeze-dried (lyophilised) antivenoms.

Though more expensive and complex to produce, these powder formulations withstand high heat and remain stable for years without cooling, needing only sterile water to reconstitute them for use.

The centuries-old process of creating antivenom is complex and relies on a method barely changed since its invention.

Reptiles at the Institute Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Pioneered in 1895 by French physician Albert Calmette in Saigon (now Ho Chi Minh), Vietnam, the process begins by manually milking live snakes for their venom.

Small, non-lethal doses are then injected into horses over several months, prompting their immune systems to produce high concentrations of specialised antibodies.

Once levels peak, blood is drawn from the horses, and the plasma is separated and purified into concentrated vials of serum.

The new breakthrough lies in a technique of lyophilisation, or freeze drying, in which the liquid serum is converted into a heat-stable powder.

The antivenom is subjected to a temperature of -40 C inside a deep vacuum chamber. It leaves a fine powder that prevents antibody proteins from degrading or clumping.

Sealed in airtight vials, the powder can sit without refrigeration for years, needing only a splash of sterile water to become an active intravenous antivenom in seconds.

Dr Isabel Batista, Museum Director Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Brazil’s antivenom infrastructure was the vision of one 19th-century physician.

The Institute’s origins trace back to 1899, when an outbreak of bubonic plague struck Santos, a major port city in the state of São Paulo, threatening Brazil’s coffee-dependent economy.

Officials turned to Dr Vital Brazil, a pioneering physician who set up a makeshift laboratory inside an old stable at Fazenda Butantan, a 400-hectare property outside the capital.

The Institute is not only sharing its life-saving sera, but its world-leading snake research Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

To test how the plague spread, he famously let himself be bitten by mosquitoes; when he didn’t fall ill, he (correctly) concluded rodents and fleas, rather than insects, were the vectors.

By 1901, the stables had officially become the Butantan Institute. The research facility was modelled on Paris’s Pasteur Institute – the “global gold-standard reference” of the era, according to Suzana Fernandes, director of the Butantan Center for Cultural Development.

“It was a model adapted here in Brazil for research, production, and the popularisation of science,” she says.

With the plague contained, Dr Brazil turned to a slower, but equally lethal threat: the pit vipers killing thousands of farmers across São Paulo’s booming coffee fields.

The snake conservation enclosure houses critically endangered species Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

While European authorities insisted a single antivenom could treat any bite, Dr Brazil proved serum must be tailored to the snake’s specific genus – a principle that remains foundational to antivenom science today.

To produce these species-specific antivenoms at scale, he devised an unconventional public barter network.

The Institute shipped wooden boxes and snake hooks to rural communities. In return, farmers captured live snakes and loaded them onto trains bound for São Paulo, where conductors guarded the locked crates in dedicated carts.

To seal the bargain, the Institute rewarded those participating with free vials of lifesaving antivenom. Between 1901 and 1977, the railway network delivered over 1.1 million live snakes to Butantan.

More than a century later, new snake lineages are still emerging from Brazil’s vast ecosystems. In 2022, for example, researchers formally described Bothrops jabrensis, a distinct species of pit viper discovered in the high-altitude forests of northeastern Paraíba.

Behind an unmarked door lies Butantan’s Herpetological Collection – one of Latin America’s most important archives of preserved reptiles.

Dr Felipe Grazziotin, curator of the Institute's herpetology collection Credit : Camila Svenson/The Telegraph

Dr Felipe Grazziotin, its curator, leads the way inside, revealing floor-to-ceiling shelves lined with stoppered glass jars. Suspended inside in pale-yellow ethanol are serpents, scorpions, and spiders – their intricate scale patterns and beady eyes frozen mid-glare.

Each jar has a handwritten label – a record of where a species was found, when and by whom. But in 2010, that priceless history was almost wiped out when a devastating fire swept through the Institute, severely damaging its collections.

Between 15,000 and 20,000 specimens were salvaged from the fire Credit : Marcelo Ribeiro Duarte/Laboratório de Coleções Zoológicas do Instituto Butantan.

Out of what was then the world’s largest snake collection – totaling nearly 100,000 specimens – scientists managed to salvage only 15,000 to 20,000. Most of the glass jars shattered in the intense heat and firefighting efforts.

“We lost more than 100 years of history about snakes in Brazil,” Dr Grazziotin says, adding that the news nearly brought him to tears at the time. “Without the label, a specimen loses its scientific meaning for us. We need to know exactly where it came from”.

A fire at the institute in 2010 severely damaged its herpetological and arachnological collections Credit : Marcelo Ribeiro Duarte/Laboratório de Coleções Zoológicas do Instituto Butantan.

He walks to the end of one of the solid metal shelves and spins a large mechanical wheel. With a low hum, the wall of jars parts down the middle, opening a new aisle.

As he steps between the banks, Dr Grazziotin points out that despite the devastation of 2010, certain parts of the collection survived the blaze remarkably intact.

“It was purely down to where they were stored in the building,” he says, gesturing toward a meticulously ordered section of jars containing some 8,000 South American rattlesnakes – an entire species’ record preserved against the odds.

Losing a century of history forced Butantan to completely rethink how it preserves its science.

Since the fire, the collection has been rebuilt inside a state-of-the-art facility with fire-suppression gas systems and shatterproof plastic containers.

In a nearby room, Dr Grazziotin proudly gestures toward a new $2 million (£1.5 million) machine: a sleek Micro-CT scanner, the only one of its kind in South America, he says.

The collection has been rebuilt inside a state-of-the-art facility with fire-suppression gas systems and shatterproof containers Credit : Camila Svenson

Rather than dissecting rare or historical specimens, it creates non-invasive “digital slices” of snake skulls and internal organs, producing detailed 3D models that can then be analysed online.

The ultimate goal, Dr Grazziotin adds, is to “digitise” the entire 120-year collection into an open-access platform.

The Butantan team is also building a network across Latin America, as well as partnerships with Portuguese-speaking African nations, including Angola and Mozambique.

“We share a language and shared experiences,” Dr Grazziotin says, lifting a nearly two-metre snake from its container. “We are bringing colleagues here to work alongside us, conducting fieldwork over there, and helping them build their own national collections”.

“The idea is to reduce regional disparities,” he adds. “If we can put all the information in our collection online, we can help scientists anywhere in the world”

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy ‘offered transfer to Brazilian giants Sao Paulo’ as former club Sheffield Wednesday seek emotional return
Sports.content:
CLUBLESS Jamie Vardy has been approached by Brazilian club Sao Paulo as his search for a new team goes on.

The Leicester legend is still assessing his options, with several English clubs also circling for his signature.



Italian reporter Fabrizio Romano was the first to break the news of Sao Paulo’s interest.

But the Englishman is reportedly still considering his options.



The Brazilian club’s approach could come as an unwanted surprise to Vardy‘s former club Sheffield Wednesday.

The Yorkshire club would love to reunite with their former player, following relegation to League One.



Wednesday’s new chairman David Storch recently revealed he would like to bring Vardy home to his boyhood club.

Storch told talkSPORT: “At some point I’ll be able to tell a story; this might not be the right time, but Jamie is somebody that we would like to have at our club.”

Vardy has drawn interest from a host of clubs, including West Ham as they begin their battle in the Championship.

The 39-year-old has been a free agent since departing then-Serie A side Cremonese at the end of June, after scoring seven goals in 29 games.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The 26-time England international has suggested he is not quite ready to retire, but did want to return to England after struggling to adapt his family to a foreign country.

This could come as a blow to Sao Paulo, with Brazil being a far longer flight from family at home in the UK and a vastly different culture too.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta warns Arsenal’s rivals they’re out to ‘win everything’ after demolishing Man City in Community Shield
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA warned that Arsenal proved their hunger for back-to-back Premier League titles by demolishing Manchester City.

Riccardo Calafiori scored after just 23 seconds in Cardiff then the Gunners added two more goals through Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard.



Skipper Odegaard said the champions “showed our level” and “want to win everything.”

Arsenal have never previously lifted successive Prem crowns.



But Arteta insists: “We know that it is going to demand something special – and we are going to go for it.

“We know what it’s going to take, we know the difficulty of the task. That’s why we’ve never done it in the club, to win it again.

“The desire comes with saying ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to live other moments even bigger than that’.

“There is more belief, we know how to do it, what it takes to win it, that was the biggest asset of the team. To play in the manner we did is extremely impressive.”

Arsenal ended the club’s 22-year wait to win the league last season and came agonisingly close to adding the Champions League – losing the final to PSG on penalties.

Skipper Odegaard said: “We showed our level. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again. We want to win everything.

“We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season. I want to score more goals.”

Several of Arteta’s players only reported back for pre season training this week but he said they were desperate to play.



Arteta added: “This win is down to the preparation that we’ve done in pre-season and the decisions that the boys have taken after the World Cup.

“They wanted to come early because they wanted to be part of this and they really wanted to win the competition”

“Fitness-wise we are not there, so you have to get there in a different way. And when you put your soul and your heart into it, that’s what happens.

“We talked about the desire that we have to start the season and to show ourselves how much we want it. I certainly saw a lot of positive things there.

“I told my players I really enjoyed watching them play. That’s a standard for us and if we drive the standards at this level, I’m sure that we’re going to be really, really competitive.”.

Goalscorer Calafiori set the Gunners on the road to victory inside the first minute and said the day could not have gone any better.

He said: “It was such an important game and test for us. It’s close to perfection this kind of performance. We wanted to show our mentality after last season.”

Sports.title: Chelsea legend backs experienced veteran duo Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to TRANSFORM Xabi Alonso’s Blues
Sports.content:
CHELSEA legend Ruud Gullit believes Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck can transform the Blues.

When superstar Gullit came to Stamford Bridge in 1995, a few months shy of his 33rd birthday, it marked the beginning of a new era for the club.



And the Dutchman says thirtysomethings Henderson and Welbeck bring the experience and authority Chelsea’s otherwise young squad has needed for so long.

Gullit said: “It’s funny. We spent so much time discussing how Chelsea lacked experience, and now they’ve added pure experience.



“Their previous issue was a complete lack of veteran presence.

“Henderson and Welbeck will be crucial in the dressing room and on the training pitch.



“They can advise younger players on what mistakes to avoid.

“Their impact isn’t just measured by matchday minutes, it’s what they do during the week.

“You need that guidance in a squad, so the signings make total sense.”

Chelsea fans spent much of last season slamming the owners and recruitment chiefs for their policy of signing mainly young players.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

6 Stamford Bridge supremo Behdad Eghbali pledged to bring in “ready-made” players to complement talent like teenage sensation Estevao.

Henderson, 36, won everything as captain of Liverpool, while Welbeck, 35, has been a Premier League striker for nearly 18 years.

Yet some Chelsea supporters are not convinced the pair are the right men to revive the club’s fortunes.

But Gullit gives BlueCo credit for recognising their mistakes and reckons Henderson and Welbeck, along with new manager Xabi Alonso, can make a real difference.

Gullit said: “The new ownership had a vision, but it failed in execution because they arrived with zero background or experience in football.

“American sports management models don’t translate directly to European football.



“They initially thought they could win exclusively with young prospects. But who guides those players when things go wrong?

“On the pitch, they looked frantic and hasty – always playing in fifth gear without any composure or ability to dictate the tempo.

“Now, appointing a manager with a strong footballing background and adding experienced players shows they are finally adjusting their philosophy.



“To win trophies, you must balance youth with experienced leaders who can guide young players.”

Gullit became Chelsea’s player-manager when Glenn Hoddle left to boss England in 1996.

The Dutchman led a team featuring Gianfranco Zola, Gianluca Vialli and Roberto di Matteo to FA Cup triumph in his first season in charge.

But Gullit was sacked in February 1998, despite the Blues enjoying another successful campaign, being following rows with then chairman Ken Bates.

Alonso is Chelsea’s SIXTH permanent boss since the BlueCo takeover in May 2022.



But Blues chiefs have vowed to give the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen head coach time to make an impact – and have given him the title of “manager” to reflect his greater influence over recruitment and the club overall.

Gullit, speaking on behalf of NY Sports Day, said: “Alonso will want to prove himself after how things ended at Real Madrid.

“He has all the qualities to be a top manager, and he brings that experience with him to London.

“Initially, I was sceptical about why he chose Chelsea given their rigid structure of handing a manager a squad and telling him to deal with it.

“But it feels as though Alonso insisted on having a direct say in recruitment before accepting the job.



“The board appears to be listening to him now rather than dictating policy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It won’t happen overnight – he needs time to evaluate a very large squad and establish his core group.”

Ruud Gullit was speaking on behalf of NY Sports Day

Sports.title: Barcelona AGREE £65.4million Rodri transfer hours after Enzo Maresca pleaded with Man City owners to make signings
Sports.content:
BARCELONA have agreed a deal worth £65.4 million for Manchester City midfielder Rodri.

The Catalan giants had seen previous bids for the 30-year-old former Ballon d’Or winner thrown out by the Prem club.



However within a couple of hours of the final whistle in the Community Shield, they struck a verbal agreement which will see them pay around £51m upfront.

And City are sure the add ons will take the fee they receive way beyond the £60m mark.



They believe it is a good deal for Rodri who has just 10 months left on his deal and has struggled with injuries over the last two years.

Maresca said in Cardiff that his team need new signings as quickly as possible after they were well beaten by Arsenal.



And they will step up the hunt for a new holding midfielder with Rodri’s move to Spain now set to be finalised in the next 48 hours.

A move for Morocco World Cup star Ayyoub Bouaddi is advanced with Lille demanding around £85 million for the teen ace.

However they will look for a direct replacement for Rodri who has spent the last seven years at the club and scored the winner in the Champions League final in 2023.

Record signing Elliot Anderson is the only new face likely to feature regularly for the first team and Maresca says there is still work to be done on the squad.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The ex-Chelsea boss said: “With any new signing, the sooner they arrive the better because we are starting the Premier League in one week.

“If they start to work with us as soon as possible it’s better that they can also understand the way we want to play.

“We knew already before the game of the things that we need to do.

“It’s not because we lost the game or even if we had won the game to think differently.



“We are quite clear in what we need to do and for sure we are going to do something before the window closes.”

There was no sign of Rodri in South Wales as talks with Barcelona continued and his absence sparked speculation a deal could be close.

The City boss said: “Rodri is a player who just won the World Cup and Ballon d’Or. He’s a top player, all the teams need Rodri so it’s not about if we miss him or not.

“The ones that played today – Elliot was quite good on his first game.”

There was also a first City appearance in 15 months for England international Jack Grealish who came on as a second half sub.



The ex Aston Villa captain is still expected to leave this month but Maresca said: “Overall I think Jack was good.

“The ones that are still here and want to work every day and if they deserve they’re going to get minutes.”

Skipper Ruben Dias admitted his team will need time to get used to life under the new boss after 10 years of playing for Pep Guardiola.

The Portugal international said: “The feeling is there’s a lot of work to put in. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working.



“There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.”

Sports.title: Scots-based millionaire leads ambitious bid to buy Premier League-winning club – and he considered buying RANGERS too
Sports.content:
A SCOTS-INDIAN businessman is plotting an ambitious swoop to buy former Premier League champions Leicester City.

Neil Lal, chairman and president of The Indian Council of the United Kingdom has put together a consortium with the aim of taking the Foxes back to their previous heights.



Thai owners King Power put the club up for sale this week, with the group expecting to rake in over £200million for the club after 16 years in charge.

And now the Scots businessman has expressed his interest in taking the reigns of the East Midlands outfit, putting in an enquiry to Leicester chiefs in writing.



Lal exclusively told SunSport: “We are looking at the Leicester situation and have written to the club for information with regards to the financials.

“Leicester City FC is a great football club with with wonderful fans.

“If things go well and both sides are happy then we plan to build the club and put it right back in the top tier of football.

“India is a country of 1.4 Billion people, we look to build bridges with different revenue streams from merchandising and streaming, which will not only increase revenue but will build bridges with new fan base on a global platform.

“These synergies are what is needed.

“We also are looking for a football venture in Scotland.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

“There shouldn’t be any changes, for example with the strip or the colours.

“In my opinion, the best thing would be to take stock of the situation, and invest in the club for better players and also to increase the revenue.

“I touched on Asia, such as India, about merchandising and streaming, as well as increasing the fanbase, I think that’s the best way forward.

“The fans, any fans, whether it’s Leicester City football club or Rangers football club or any football club, that’s the heart and soul, and at the end of the day, we need to build the club to where it should be, which is the top tier of football.”

Lal and his group don’t just have their sights set on Leicester though.



He’s admitting that one day they’d LOVE to take control of Rangers.

Lal admitted that it might be soon to launch a takeover bid for the Ibrox club however, with the US 49ers Enterprises freshly in post.

But he has ambitious plans if he ever does get his hands on the Light Blues.



He continued: “In Scotland the two largest clubs are Rangers and Celtic.

“We are currently looking at the situation and feel that Rangers FC have the potential to do much better and on the pitch and financially.

“Once again by increasing the revenue stream with regards to merchandise and streaming on a global scale with India, this will provide more funds to invest in players and to increase the stadium capacity too, which will pay in the long run.

“From a 50,000 stadium to 60,000 or more will bring in more revenue. Football has rules and you can only invest on new players depending on your revenue.

“There is much improvement that can be done here. If the opportunity arises to invest in Rangers or another club we shall explore that situation when it comes.



“The issue with football is Scotland is the that financial revenue are low compared to England.

“However with expanding fan base on a global scale clubs can increase there revenue.

“Obviously, the new owners have taken over and it has not been easy, they’ve spent a lot of money.

“In my opinion, I would rather buy their stake in full if it comes up that it is available, and if it’s at the right price that suits us.

“Working in partnership is a possibility, however, I would prefer to buy the full stake for our plans.



“What we would plan is to increase the capacity of the stadium, you have the gap sides, you can dig under too, so we could expand it to at least 60,000 or more, that’s one mission.

“A hotel can also be built, which would increase more revenue with people staying at the games, with a restaurant there too.

“There are many other things that can be done too, but these are the two options.



“If the opportunity came up, we would buy the full stake, but right now it’s a bit too early, it’s not been easy for them, but if the opportunity did come up, and it’s got to be the right price, we would buy the full stake from them.

“Lets see what happens, we have a vision and we’re here for the long term – we’re not here to make a quick buck and get out.

“India is an integral part to that, Asia in general, it’s all about merchandising, streaming, it’s a global fanbase.

“It’s the way forward because of the Fair Play rules, so that is the way forward.”

Neither Scots-born Lal nor his consortium have experience working in football.



So ensure the footballing side of operations would run smoothly is simple – leave it to the experts.

He added: “I’m not a footballer, I’m a football fan, but I’m not a footballer and we should leave that to the people that know the game inside out, we’re businessmen, that’s what we are.

“We should hire the best people possible for the roles and also to take it further, I think we should involve the ex-footballers and have a committee who understand the game, on the buying and selling too, and take their advice.

“Myself and the consortium are not involved in football.

Yes, we are businessmen, yes, we are football fans, but we will not be running the football club as the CEO for example.



“We will hire the best people for the job, which is the correct way to do things and I think that’s the best way forward.

“What happens is, when you have people who are owners of football clubs, they get a bit emotional, they make mistakes, but I believe we should leave it to the experts

“If I’m a baker, and someone asked me to become a florist I wouldn’t have a clue, so there’s no point in me doing that.”

Lal already has connections with Rangers, as he awarded the Ibrox club the Indian Council Community Cohesion Award in 2022 on behalf of the Scottish Indian council.

Speaking at the time, he said: “We commend the Managing Director, Stewart Robertson, and the board of Rangers FC for their commitment to ensure people of all backgrounds and cultures can enjoy football in a safe and tolerant atmosphere.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The leadership and commitment shown by Rangers FC for their ground-breaking diversity and inclusion campaign, ‘Everyone Anyone’ is worthy of the highest praise.”

Sports.title: Lethargic Luke Shaw’s display vs AC Milan shows Michael Carrick can’t afford to gamble with Man Utd’s left-back crisis
Sports.content:
LUKE SHAW’S shaky display against AC Milan showed that Michael Carrick cannot afford to gamble with Manchester United’s left-back crisis.

The Red Devils’ grim performance in the friendly against the Italians was a brutal reminder of the glaring issues that need fixing over the next fortnight.



Former gaffer Ruben Amorim famously spoke about the club needing to “suffer” before the glory days returned.

And his Milan side certainly made United suffer in Wroclaw. Despite going in front twice — through Harry Maguire after just two minutes and Patrick Dorgu — they were well beaten 4-2.



That pain is spilling into the transfer market, where the Red Devils are miles off their rivals in summer spending. It will inevitably have consequences this season.

United are the only so-called traditional Premier League ‘Big Six’ club never to have spent £100million on a single player.

This summer Chelsea have splashed £117m on Morgan Rogers, City handed £116m over for Elliot Anderson and Tottenham spent a combined £185m on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Much was made of United bolstering their midfield this summer but now it is apparent how desperate they are for a new left-back.

Amorim’s Milan, using the 3-4-2-1 system that proved a woeful fit at Old Trafford, blew United away in the second half.

Samuel Chukwueze — who spent last term on loan at Fulham — ran riot at right wing-back, scoring one and then setting up goals for Alphadjo Cisse and Goncalo Ramos with two identical crosses from Shaw’s side.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

On each occasion, Shaw shuffled across too slowly. While Amorim’s formation naturally leaves defenders vulnerable on the flanks, the lapse highlights why United are actively considering fresh investment in that position.

Ruben Loftus-Cheek nabbed Milan’s fourth in Poland.

Carrick (left) revealed he “needs” more players before the September 1 deadline when speaking to journalists in Dublin.

At 31 and entering his final year at Old Trafford, 2014 signing Shaw cannot carry the load alone given his injury history.



He was excellent last season, starting all 38 Prem matches, but that was a one-game-per-week schedule and United are back in the Champions League this term.

That is why United have looked at Newcastle’s Lewis Hall, Myles Lewis-Skelly, 19, at Arsenal and others.

Hall is the ultimate target, but United had two initial enquiries rejected by Toon bosses.

Unless the 21-year-old forces an exit and the Old Trafford hierarchy slap down a mega-money offer, any deal is highly unlikely.

With left-back Harry Amass, 19, set to leave this summer, United lack strength in depth.



Shaw played the entire 90 minutes against Milan, his first full game of pre-season, and the heat played a part in a low-energy second half from United. Relying exclusively on Shaw — solid but not as pacy as he used to be — presents a massive risk.

United tried to solve their full-back issue when Dorgu joined as Amorim’s first signing — the former Lecce star was designed to fit the Portuguese’s system as a wing-back.

Dorgu has been used as a left-winger by Carrick, with Marcus Rashford also back in the team for now. As the club’s highest earner, Rashford is a factor in why United’s transfer business has stalled since Youri Tielemans’ £35m arrival from Aston Villa.

Ironically, finishing 15th afforded Amorim greater spending power than Carrick enjoys for guiding United to third.

Amorim was backed last summer to try to get United into the Champions League through the signings of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko for £207.5m.



So far, under Carrick, United have committed £85m — Tielemans and the £50m addition from Chelsea, Andrey Santos — even though they are back in Europe’s elite competition.

United’s engine room lacks an engine. Kobbie Mainoo’s return is a relief but they still need a runner to cover ground and mask Tielemans’ lack of athleticism.

Noticing familiar United reporters, Amorim could not resist a nod to his volatile media moments. He grinned: “Did you miss me?” We miss your press conferences,” came the reply. “More boring now,” Amorim laughed.

A punchline that applies just as neatly to United’s subdued transfer window.

Sports.title: Como star suffers sickening injury in Liverpool friendly as commentator apologises to fans eating their lunch
Sports.content:
COMO star Alberto Dossena suffered a horror injury during his side’s friendly with Liverpool.

The Italian, 27, dislocated his finger in the sickening moment during a behind-closed-doors friendly at Liverpool‘s AXA training ground on Saturday.



The 70-minute game was temporarily halted after the defender fell awkwardly while challenging for a header with James McConnell and Will Wright.

And after landing on his hand to break his fall it was clear Dossena had suffered a very nasty injury.



Even LFCTV commentator John Bradley was left horrified and apologised to any watching fans who were “having their lunch”.

He said : “That’s a nasty landing. We might need a little stoppage here to get the medical team on.



“Well yes there you go, he’s dislocated his finger.”

Co-commentator Natasha Dowie then said: “Woah that’s not nice.”

Bradley added: “Apologies if you are just trying to have your lunch or if you’re in, who knows, San Diego having a very early breakfast.

“Sometimes you just see things that make you squirm.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta ‘fighting with the Premier League’ to make rule change as he admits ‘sadness’ at leaving players out
Sports.content:
ARSENAL boss Mikel Arteta has revealed he’s fighting the Premier League about the size of matchday squads.

The Spaniard was left disappointed after being forced to leave players out of his Community Shield squad and has called for the Prem to allow more spaces.



Speaking after his side’s 3-0 demolition of Man City, Arteta pointed to two players he was gutted to not have in the squad on Sunday.

He said to TNT Sports: “It’s really sad not to have their availability. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend and accommodate more players in the squad because they deserve to be in the squad, there’s no question.



“Ethan [Nwaneri] and Marli [Salmon] as well, who has had the whole pre-season with us. Hopefully we can change that rule so players can enjoy on the pitch and can be an option to play and contribute to the team going forward.”

Arteta’s squad omissions led to speculation about some players’ futures.

Brazilian duo Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli were also not included in Sunday’s clash.

When asked if they will remain Arsenal players in this transfer window, Arteta replied: “Yes they’re very important for us.”

Despite Arteta’s comments, Nwaneri, who spent part of last season on loan at Marseille, is reportedly expected to depart Arsenal before the end of the summer window.

The BBC claim that the 19-year-old has interest from abroad – with AC Milan, RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund keen – and from Fulham in the Prem.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Martinelli, meanwhile, was the subject of a bid from Galatasaray, although the winger has rejected a move to Turkey.

Despite Arteta’s qualms about who he could and couldn’t put in the squad, it didn’t prove to be a problem for the Gunners, who started the season how they will mean to go on.

A quick start saw Riccardo Calafiori score the quickest goal in Community Shield history after just 23 SECONDS, following Myles Lewis-Skelly’s gilt-edged ball through.

And captain Martin Odegaard’s 48th minute finish cued the start of the celebrations as Arsenal stormed into a 3-0 lead.



During the actual celebrations, midfield general Declan Rice hilariously hit himself in the face with the trophy, as he enjoyed a moment with the fans.

Arsenal begin their season on Friday, as Premier League newbies Coventry make the trip to the Emirates.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Barcelona agree Rodri deal, Liverpool's Barcola boost, £60m for Arsenal to sign star
Sports.content:
All of the latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester United, Tottenham and more

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's transfer live blog for Sunday, August 16.

Liverpool have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola as a result of Paris Saint-Germain signing Mika Godts from Ajax. There was speculation that the Ligue 1 champions would be willing to trim their £145million valuation of the 23-year-old, but only if they secured a solid replacement on the left.

Savinho, meanwhile, has reportedly shared an interest in working under Roberto De Zerbi this season, with Spurs looking to wrap up an £85m move for the Brazilian.

At the Etihad Stadium, the Cityzens are on the brink of securing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in an £85m swoop of their own, as Rodri closes in on a move to Barcelona after the clubs finally agreed terms. Having already welcomed Elliot Anderson in a £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, City have now turned their attention to finding a suitable playing partner for the 23-year-old.

Bouaddi, 18, could be just that, following a formidable World Cup campaign with Morocco.

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to change tack in transfer market to match Chelsea and Man City
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to change tack in transfer market to match Chelsea and Man City

Manchester United's record when it comes to selling players has left a lot of be desired in recent years, but Old Trafford chiefs hope to drive up sales with their new strategy

View 3 Images Radek Vitek recently left Manchester United (Image: Chris Vaughan/Getty Images)

Manchester United are attempting to monetise their academy in a bid to match their Premier League rivals. The Red Devils are putting a greater emphasis on young talent, not only with a view to strengthen their first-team but also improve the club's finances.

‌



It's a strategy that has already seen highly rated goalkeeper Radek Vitek leave on a permanent basis, despite an impressive loan spell with Bristol City last season and United's lack of depth in the goalkeeping department. Vitek, 22, was sold to Middlesbrough in a deal rising to £14million, with United inserting a 35 per cent sell-on clause plus a buy back option.

‌



The Mail report that United acknowledge the view that their historic conveyor belt has slowed over the past few years, while the likes of Manchester City and Chelsea have made millions from their academy products. It's added that 19-year-old left-back Harry Amass could be sold for roughly £7m plus add-ons before deadline day on September 1.

‌



Meanwhile, 22-year-old midfielder Toby Collyer is understood to be available. Fans may question the idea of offloading youngsters ahead of a season in which Michael Carrick's side will play at least 48 matches, having qualified for the Champions League.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher tells Man City to call off transfer immediately after Arsenal drubbing
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher tells Man City to call off transfer immediately after Arsenal drubbing

Arsenal dominated Manchester City as they beat Enzo Maresca's side 3-0 in the Community Shield at the Principality Stadium on Sunday afternoon

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher sent a transfer message to Manchester City during their Community Shield defeat to Arsenal (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Jamie Carragher has told Manchester City they must keep Rodri after watching Arsenal run riot in the Community Shield. The Gunners set a marker for the new season with a comfortable 3-0 victory over Enzo Maresca’s side in Cardiff.

‌



But new City boss Maresca omitted Rodri and Savinho as transfer speculation continues to surround them. Even though City have stated they want Rodri to stay and sign a new deal, it has become clear that he wants to leave, with Barcelona his preferred destination.

‌



The Catalan giants stepped up their interest in the midfielder earlier this week by making a second bid worth more than £51million. But as previously reported, City are asking for at least £70m for the World Cup winner.

‌



But as Carragher watched Maresca’s side come up short against the Premier League champions, the former Liverpool defender made clear he thinks that City need to cancel any talks to let Rodri leave. Taking to X, he wrote: “Arsenal 3-0. Man City have to keep Rodri.”

However, shortly after Carragher's post, Fabrizio Romano claimed that the Spaniard is closing in on a move to Barcelona after City 'gave the green light' to their latest offer.

On Sunday, Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after just 24 seconds for the Gunners before Kai Havertz added a second with a close-range header. Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard then wrapped up the win with a clever finish just three minutes after the break.

‌

Rodri has entered the final 12 months of his City deal, and speaking in his pre-Arsenal press conference, Maresca updated on the Spaniard’s future, saying 'anything can happen' as long as the transfer window is open.

And speaking after his side’s defeat at the Principality Stadium, the new City boss said: "I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment.

“I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated."

Sports.title: World Cup final referee's unheard plea to Lionel Messi exposed in new footage
Sports.content:
World Cup final referee's unheard plea to Lionel Messi exposed in new footage

Spain prevailed in a fiery World Cup final where referee Slavko Vincic pleaded with Lionel Messi over some of Argentina's second-half antics in the United States

View 2 Images Referee Slavko Vincic speaks to Lionel Messi during the World Cup final (Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

World Cup referee Slavko Vincic pleaded with Lionel Messi to calm down his out-of-control team-mate Leandro Paredes during the tournament's final. The Argentina captain was tasked with keeping Paredes on the field before the violent scenes he sparked come the full-time whistle.

‌



Paredes spotted kicking and punching as he shoved Spain star Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Barcelona ace Gavi. The 32-year-old only entered the match at half-time, but was fortunate to stay on the pitch.

‌



The former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder picked up a yellow card after just six minutes on the pitch for a nasty foul and spent the remainder of the match living on the edge as Enzo Fernandez was sent off. Paredes' antics prompted on-field official Vincic to attempt to take mitigating action through Messi, though that did not prevent the shenanigans at full time.

‌



Footage has emerged from referee cam in which Vincic can be heard warning Messi that Paredes was riding his luck on the field. "Messi, control Paredes," he could be heard saying.

"I don't want to...he has yellow. Control please. Always, always."

Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing READ MORE :

FIFA opened disciplinary proceedings against Paredes for his shameful post-match actions. The world football governing body has alleged three counts of assault against the player.

‌



Argentina's Nahuel Molina has also come under the spotlight for two counts of assault and team coach Roberto Ayala for one count. Molina appeared to strike Rodri while Ayala hit Dani Olmo.

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente was left in disbelief with what transpired. "At the time, I didn't realise it. I was celebrating, hugging team-mates," De La Fuente told Spanish television.

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has been charged by FIFA due to the incident after the World Cup final vs Spain (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.

"I want to highlight our behaviour in the face of that kind of aggression and provocation. Our players always kept their composure and behaved like true professionals."

‌



Paredes was caught up in more drama upon his return to club football. The veteran sparked more uproar for Boca Juniors when he kicked the ball at an opponent.

As a Central Cordoba player looked to get to his feet following a foul, Paredes kicked the ball towards him, though how deliberate it was remains up for debate. Paredes was only on the field for 14 minutes.

Sports.title: Arsenal deliver painful Enzo Maresca reality check as Man City on end of mauling
Sports.content:
Arsenal deliver painful Enzo Maresca reality check as Man City on end of mauling

ARSENAL 3-0 MANCHESTER CITY: Enzo Maresca's first big outing since replacing Pep Guardiola turned into a nightmare in Cardiff as City's title rivals ran riot

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca endured a painful afternoon at the hands of Arsenal (Image: Glyn Kirk/AFP)

Arsenal dished out a mauling to Enzo Maresca in his first test since replacing Pep Guardiola. And a painful reminder to Manchester City of just how tough life is going to be without the Spanish genius.

‌



These two teams were the best in the Premier League last season. But in one game in Cardiff's Principality Stadium, the bitter rivals looked poles apart. Arsenal ripped City to shreds from start to finish, including an opening goal inside 23 seconds, on an afternoon Maresca will want to forget in a hurry.

‌



But the pressure on the Italian to maintain the incredible standards his predecessor set, will never escape him. As for Mikel Arteta, he waited three years to end his trophy drought, and has now pocketed two inside four months.

‌



Riccardo Califiori opened the scoring within half a minute - and Arsenal never looked back. Kai Havertz doubled the lead, before the impressive Martin Odegaard completed the rout in style.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

There was £125m worth of new talent on show, in the shape of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Elliot Anderson, while Jack Grealish was named on the City bench.

‌



There was no Rodri for City, though, with the Spanish World Cup winner still at the centre of a transfer saga between his club and Barcelona. And it took Maresca's men just 23 seconds to miss the glue Rodri provides and come unstuck.

Miles Lewis-Skelly turned past Phil Foden and slipped a sublime pass inside Ruben Dias for Calafiori to run onto and beat Gianluigi Donnarumma with a neat finish. Welcome to the new job, Enzo.

Arsenal looked pumped up, and moments later Odegaard charged forward but somehow the move came to nothing, despite him having options left and right.

‌



City looked disjointed and sluggish. It took them 20 minutes to show signs of life, when Foden demanded a smart save from David Raya with a dripping strike. Gabriel had to snuff out a dangerous run from Jeremy Doku minutes later. The Brazilian then puffed out his chest and pumped up the crowd.

View 2 Images Arsenal ran riot to condemn Manchester City to a bruising defeat (Image: Getty Images)

It felt like this game meant more to Arsenal than City. So it came as no surprise when Arteta's men doubled their lead before half time. Odegaard picked out Tzolis at the back post and when he headed it back into the path of Havertz, the German managed to bundle his own header past a flapping Donnarumma.

‌



City had a mountain to climb. Scoring one past this Arsenal defence looked beyond them, let alone three. Especially when City started creating chances, but missed them. Erling Haaland should have beaten Raya, but saw his shot well saved, before Ben White produced a stunning block to deflect Doku's shot over the crossbar.

Califiori should have made it 3-0 at the opposite end, but volleyed over from close range, while Josko Gvardiol hacked a shot from Odegaard off his own line.

It got that desperate, Maresca sent on Grealish for the second half. But the first action he saw was Odegaard putting Donnarumma on his backside in the process of making it 3-0, to pile more pain on City. Maresca was taunted with chants of 'you're getting sacked in the morning'.

‌



Just one of the past 15 winners of this silverware have gone on to become champions that season.

But on this evidence, Arsenal look more than capable of bucking the trend.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement statement - 'It's all mapped out'

Cristiano Ronaldo has entered the last year of his contract with Al-Nassr after playing his final World Cup with Portugal, and the 41-year-old has opened up on his future plans

View 2 Images Retirement is near for Cristiano Ronaldo (Image: Stacy Revere/Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has dropped a bombshell and revealed that this season will 'probably' his last. Ronaldo, 41, only has one year left on his mega-money contract with Al-Nassr, having previously admitted that he's in the final knockings of his prestigious career.

‌



The Portugal captain played at his sixth and final World Cup over the summer, as his nation crashed out in the quarter-finals with a 1-0 loss against eventual champions Spain. Speaking for the first time since Portugal's heartbreak in an interview with Vogue Magazine, Ronaldo has suggested that this season will be his last.

‌



"This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy," he stated. "I have my future all mapped out. I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard.

‌



"Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one. And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I've earned - what we've earned. Because after all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."

The interview took place five days before Ronaldo married his long-term partner, Georgina Rodriguez, in an intimate ceremony at their home in Cascais, Portugal. Earlier this week, the former Manchester United megastar returned to Saudi Arabia but didn't feature in Al-Nassr's opening game of the season.

The Saudi champions began their title defence with a 3-0 victory over Al-Fateh under new manager Ange Postecoglou. Their former boss, Jorge Jesus, left at the end of last season and is now Portugal's head coach.

Speaking at his unveiling press conference, Jesus said that the door was open for Ronaldo to receive a call-up, with their next match scheduled for late September. "I haven't spoken to Cris yet. He will never be a problem for the national team or for me," Jesus explained.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sends clear transfer message to three Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sends clear transfer message to three Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield

Mikel Arteta has made it clear where a group of fringe players stand ahead of the 2026/27 season by naming his squad for the Community Shield against Manchester City

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's squad selection for the Community Shield told a story (Image: Ryan Pierse/The FA via Getty Images)

Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri have been sent a clear message by Mikel Arteta after being left out of the Arsenal squad for the Community Shield.

‌



Arsenal play Manchester City in the season-opener at Wembley on Sunday afternoon following a difficult pre-season campaign. There are still 16 days left in the summer transfer window - and Arteta's selection has sent a message to his fringe players.

‌



While new signings Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis have come into the starting XI immediately following their arrival, others have been given the cold shoulder.

‌



Arsenal starting XI vs Man City: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly, Guimaraes, Odegaard, Madueke, Tzolis, Havertz.

Substitutes: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Zubimendi, Merino, Rice, Eze, Dowman, Saka, Gyokeres.

Martinelli, Jesus and Nwaneri have all been linked with transfers in this window and it seems that is the plan. None are involved at Wembley, while Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice have been left on the bench, having returned late for pre-season following their involvement with England at the World Cup.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) are the only players have left Arsenal for transfer fees this summer and Arteta knows that time is running out.

Galatasaray want to sign Martinelli for €45million (£38m), but the striker is reportedly not keen on moving to Turkey. The Brazilian forward has been with the Gunners since 2019 but has entered the final year of his contract in north London.

‌



Napoli have been in talks to sign Jesus, who is also in the final 12 months of his contract and has fallen down the pecking order behind Kai Havertz, who starts against Man City, and Viktor Gyokeres, who is named on the bench.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli is on the transfer list (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Jesus is expected to join Napoli for around £17m once they have shifted Romelu Lukaku and Lorenzo Lucca. He will join former Manchester United frontman Rasmus Hojlund in Italy if he does move in the coming weeks.

‌



Nwaneri has also interested Galatasaray, who have even suggested a potential swap deal involving star striker Victor Osimhen. The 19-year-old midfielder is also of interest to AC Milan, Fulham, Red Bull Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund, according to BBC Sport.

Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta is the man tasked with finding new clubs for the group of unwanted players. Reiss Nelson is expected to leave, while Fabio Vieira is also on the transfer list.

Arteta is excited to see his new signings play against City. "Christos came early so that always helps. Bruno joined us last week. He's in good condition and we know what he will bring to the team," he told TNT Sports.

Article continues below

Asked about bringing back players after the World Cup, he added: "It is something very individual. Declan played over 65 games; he needed complete rest and we have to build him up. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that's good to see as well."

Sports.title: Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing
Sports.content:
Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing

Norwich City winger Matej Jurasek joined Sparta Prague on a season-long loan earlier this week, but endured a hostile reception from his new club's fans

View 2 Images Sparta Prague's players and supporters clashed over the signing of Matej Jurasek on Saturday night

Sparta Prague coach Brian Priske was forced to step in after Matej Jurasek endured a hostile reception from fans of his new club. Jurasek joined Sparta on a season-long loan from Norwich City earlier this week and made his debut against FK Teplice off the bench on Saturday.

‌



But supporters of Sparta have clearly not forgotten Jurasek’s past with rivals Slavia Prague. Their anger reportedly stems in part from footage from the winger’s time at Slavia in which he appeared in a balaclava while joining anti-Sparta chants.

‌



Even though he was only on the pitch for the final 15 minutes, his every touch was booed, and he was the subject of chants that said 'we don't want you here'. His side’s post-match lap of appreciation was cut short amid the abuse directed towards the winger.

‌



Jurasek did engage in conversation with that section of supporters, telling them: "I'm a young player and I came here to win. I apologise for the statements I made against your club."

Then, after the game, Sparta coach Priske, along with a number of his players, approached his side’s supporters to defend Jurasek. Speaking to Oneplay Sport afterwards, Priske said: "It is clear that the arrival of Matej has caused a lot of reactions in the Czech Republic.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Content cannot be displayed without consent

“We all expected it and knew that there would be different opinions around him. These are of course always welcome, as long as they are expressed in a decent way.

‌



"He knew that coming to Sparta would mean enormous pressure and would provoke strong reactions. Nevertheless, he decided to come with one goal - to help us.

“From the conversations we had together, I know that he is well aware of the whole situation and knows that he is not in a very good position with some of the fans at the moment.

View 2 Images Matej Jurasek in action for Norwich City against Stoke City last season (Image: (David Watts/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

‌



"It gave Matej a chance to express his feelings and apologise to many Spartans. It was a good moment to let out all the emotions that had built up over the past few days."

Jurasek featured in Norwich's first competitive game of the season, having come off the bench in their Carabao Cup first-round win against League One side MK Dons last week. And Sparta will have the option to make the Czech Republic international's move permanent at the end of the season.

"I think those 15 or 20 minutes today showed why we brought him in. Now it's up to him. He has to prove to the fans that he's one of us," Priske added.

Article continues below

"His job is to do everything he can to make sure that all those amazing Spartan fans are chanting his name next year for a completely different reason and in a positive spirit."

Sports.title: GB denied 2028 Olympics spot as USA and Canada win flag football world titles
Sports.content:
The United States successfully defended the men's title at the flag football world championships on Sunday but lost the women's title to Canada, while Mexico's women and Canada's men earned qualification spots for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

The US men's team beat Italy 46-26 to secure a sixth straight title, while the women's side missed out on a fourth straight after losing 27-20 to Canada.

"Gold is the only standard," said US men's quarterback Nico Casares, who threw two touchdown passes. "That's our motto. That's what we play by, that's what we live by."

Flag football: Rules of the game In 2023, flag football was among five sports given Olympic status for the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. The game is played five-on-five in two 20-minute halves, with no tackling and an emphasis on speed and elusiveness. The NFL has said it plans to launch women's and men's professional flag football ahead of the Olympics.

The US women's side started strongly but it was tied 14-14 at the break after Caroline Moquin-Joubert caught Canada quarterback Sara Parker's pass at the end of the first half.

Parker then set up Frederique Morneau at the start of the second half as Canada took control.

Image: Canada's women's team celebrate their flag football world title that also clinched their spot at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028

The US had a fourth down, yards from the line, with three seconds left, but could not make the final play count. It was Canada's third title and first since beating the US in the 2014 final.

The top two men's and women's teams outside of the US men's and women's teams - because they already qualified as hosts - also earned spots at the 2028 Olympic Games.

Sunday's two other finalists - the Italian men and Canadian women - earned their place by reaching the final against the US teams, meaning that the bronze-medal games decided who joined them.

Mexico women cried with joy after a 20-19 win over Great Britain - who rallied from 20-6 down - for the women's bronze and an Olympic spot.

But Mexico's men lost 34-26 in overtime to Canada, who claimed an Olympic spot.
